name: Brookfield
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Brookfield, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Brookfield, IL: free trolleys, Santa on a fire truck, the Kris Kringle Market and the tree lighting at historic Grossdale Station.
lede: Brookfield starts the season with one big December afternoon: free trolleys loop through town, Santa rolls in on a fire truck, and the village tree lights up beside Grossdale Station, the train depot built in 1889.
celebrates: The Holiday Celebration, put on by the Village and the Brookfield Chamber of Commerce, has run for many decades and is how most local families open the season. Free trolleys loop through the downtown and Broadway Avenue business districts, stopping at Village Hall, the Linda Sokol Francis Brookfield Public Library, S.E. Gross Middle School and blocks of local shops. Kids find hot chocolate, crafts in the library's Maker Studio, a petting zoo, an iceless skating rink and Santa and Mrs. Claus. The Chamber's Kris Kringle Market fills Village Hall with local makers and young entrepreneurs. The day ends at Historic Grossdale Station, now the permanent home of the tree lighting.
lastyear: Brookfield's 2025 Holiday Celebration was planned for Saturday, Dec. 6, from 2 to 6 p.m. The Kris Kringle Market, in its third year, was set to stretch across the whole weekend at Village Hall with more than 70 vendors and a new Gift of Giving Tree that collected food and winter clothing. Plans called for trolleys among six stops, the library poured hot chocolate, and S.E. Gross Middle School had a giant inflatable snow globe plus its holiday band and choir. At 5 p.m. Riverside-Brookfield High School carolers sang until Santa arrived by fire truck for the 5:30 p.m. countdown.
facts: Grossdale Station opened in 1889. Developer Samuel Eberly Gross spent $5,000 on it to convince the Chicago, Burlington and Quincy Railroad to stop at his new subdivision, Grossdale, and an ad of the time called it the finest suburban station on the line. When the railroad planned to tear it down in 1977, residents formed the Brookfield Historical Society to save it, and on April 9, 1981 the depot was rolled across the tracks to its current spot. Each fall the Village asks residents to donate a pine or fir to stand beside it as the holiday tree.
trains: Brookfield has three stops on the Metra BNSF line between Chicago Union Station and Aurora: Hollywood, known as the Hollywood/Zoo Stop, then Brookfield on Burlington Avenue, then Congress Park. From Hollywood/Zoo it is about half a mile, roughly a 10 minute walk, to the main entrance of Brookfield Zoo Chicago, where Holiday Magic has lit up December nights for 45 years. The 1889 Grossdale depot now holds the Brookfield Historical Museum. For a bigger train day, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union and the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin both run Christmas rides.

traditions: Free trolleys loop all afternoon between Village Hall, the library, S.E. Gross Middle School and the business districts.
The Chamber's market at Village Hall gathers local makers, food vendors and kids from the Young Entrepreneurs program.
At the market, Santa's elves help kids write letters, and every letter gets a reply from the North Pole.
Santa arrives at Grossdale Station on a fire truck and leads the crowd in counting down to light the village tree.
Brookfield Zoo Chicago runs Chicagoland's longest running holiday lights festival, with more than 3.5 million lights.
kidfact: Brookfield used to be called Grossdale, after the man who built its first train station in 1889. The town changed its name in 1905, but the old station is still there, and that is where the Christmas tree glows every year.
faq: Where is the Brookfield Christmas tree lighting?

It happens at Historic Grossdale Station, 8820 1/2 Brookfield Avenue, which shares a trolley stop with Village Hall. The Riverside-Brookfield Landmark reported in 2025 that the station is now the permanent home of the tree lighting. It closes out the Holiday Celebration, with high school carolers first and then Santa arriving on a fire truck to lead the countdown.
Is the Brookfield Holiday Celebration free?

Yes. Walking around, riding the trolleys and most of the activities are free, and parking in the business districts is free during the event. In past years kids have found free hot chocolate, crafts at the library, a petting zoo and an iceless rink. Shops and Kris Kringle Market vendors sell gifts and food, so bring a little money for treats.
Where can kids meet Santa in Brookfield?

During the 2025 Holiday Celebration, Santa and Mrs. Claus heard wish lists and posed for family photos at Irish Times on Burlington Avenue, and Santa's elves helped kids write letters at the Kris Kringle Market. Santa then rode a fire truck to Grossdale Station for the tree lighting. Brookfield Zoo Chicago also has Santa visits during Holiday Magic.
Can we take Metra to Brookfield for Christmas events?

Yes. Brookfield has three Metra BNSF stations: Hollywood/Zoo, Brookfield at 8858 Burlington Avenue, and Congress Park. The Brookfield station is the closest to downtown, Village Hall and Grossdale Station. The Hollywood/Zoo Stop is about a 10 minute walk from the main entrance of Brookfield Zoo Chicago, which makes it an easy train trip for Holiday Magic.

The Village of Brookfield and the Brookfield Chamber of Commerce co-sponsor the Holiday Celebration, and the Chamber runs the Kris Kringle Market. Local businesses host stops along the trolley route, the library hosts crafts, and S.E. Gross Middle School opens its gym. The Village says the event keeps a small town feel that many young families value.
What is at Grossdale Station during the celebration?

The 1889 depot is home to the Brookfield Historical Museum, run by the Brookfield Historical Society. In 2025 the museum was open until 4 p.m. on celebration day, and woodcarvers gave live demonstrations outside until 5 p.m. Families can see the old station up close before the crowd gathers for the tree lighting.
